replies: First question: "Walk me through your resume — why finance, and why this role?" Answer as you would in the interview (speak in full sentences, 60–90 seconds). When you post your answer here I'll score it on structure, evidence and specificity and give one concrete improvement, then ask the next question.

Score: 4/10.

Why: It's short and technical but misses the interviewer's prompt. They asked for "Walk me through your resume — why finance, and why this role?" Your reply describes a task you might do (building a model) not your career story, motivations, or specific experiences that prove you can do it.

One concrete improvement: use the 3-part structure the review recommended—(1) quick background that led you to finance, (2) two concrete experiences that show relevant skills (what you did, the result with a number), (3) why this role at this firm matches your goals—then tie it to the job. Keep it ~60–90s.

Rewritten example you can adapt (about 75 seconds):
"I studied [major] at [school], where I first got interested in finance during an internship analyzing revenue trends for a regional retailer. There I built a three‑statement model from revenue-driver assumptions and used it to recommend product focus changes that the team adopted. After that I worked as a financial analyst at [company], where I automated variance analyses and improved forecasting accuracy by [X%], which saved the FP&A team [hours/month] and tightened monthly guidance. I'm excited about this financial analyst role at [firm] because you focus on [public markets/consumer/PE-backed companies], and my hands-on modeling, forecasting and dashboarding can help the team improve
guidance and evaluate opportunities. In short: education that led to finance, concrete results in modeling and forecasting, and a clear match to this role."

Next question (after you revise or confirm): "Tell me about a time you found an error in a model or report. What did you do and what happened?"

You gave a single-sentence technical reply that didn't answer the prompt. Honest score: 3/10.

Why: 
- It ignored the question ("Walk me through your resume — why finance, and why this role?") and instead described a task. 
- No structure (background → experiences → fit). 
- No concrete examples, metrics, or timeline to prove capability. 
- Tone is terse and not narrative—interviewers need concise stories, not commands.
One clear fix to make now:
Use this 3-part structure and expand to ~60–90 seconds:
1) Brief background that explains how you got into finance.
2) Two concrete experiences (one internship or class project; one job) with what you did and a measurable result.
3) Why this firm/role fits (mention one thing about the firm and the skill you bring).
Rewrite you can use (fill brackets): 
"I studied [major] at [school], where I got into finance through [class/internship]. In my internship at [firm], I built a three‑statement model from revenue drivers and used it to recommend [action], which led to [result, % or $]. At [current/last job], I improved forecasting accuracy by [X%] by automating variance analyses, saving the team [hours/month]. I want this financial analyst role at [company] because you focus on [area], and my modeling and forecasting experience will help the team [specific impact]."

Next step: Do you want me to score and improve your rewrite if you paste it?
